summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a homeless man with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic alcohol and polysubstance use, was admitted after being found in an alley with chest pain following a reported assault where he was punched near his implantable defibrillator and had his medications stolen. He had consumed a large amount of vodka that morning and experienced hypoglycemia, which resolved with treatment. Evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction, with negative troponins and a normal EKG, and imaging showed no acute cardiopulmonary issues. He was managed for alcohol withdrawal using CIWA-guided diazepam and symptom control. Despite medical recommendations, he became impatient with care, declined further observation, and left against medical advice. His chronic conditions remained stable, and he was advised to resume his home medications and follow up with cardiology and primary care.
problems: Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Alcoholic gastritis, without mention of hemorrhage
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, continuous
